rows: An utterance that performs an action rather than describes one
The act of saying something with a definite sense and reference
What the speaker is doing in making the utterance (the force)
The causal effect on the hearer
Conditions that must hold for a speech act to succeed
Failure of A or B conditions — act simply doesn't occur
Failure of Γ conditions — act occurs but is insincere
Speech act committing speaker to truth of a proposition
Speech act attempting to get hearer to do something
Speech act committing speaker to future action
Speech act that brings about the state of affairs it names
"X counts as Y in C" — rule that creates the activity
